QF.id: VIII Introduction to Forwards and Futures_70

question.text: A trader is short 2 lots of stock futures at Rs. 1,800. Lot size is 400. Day 1 settlement is Rs. 1,760. What is the MTM?

explanation.text: The Logic: A short position gains when the settlement price falls below the entry price. Per-share gain for the short = 1,800 - 1,760 = Rs. 40. Per-lot gain = 40 x 400 = Rs. 16,000. Total gain for 2 lots = 16,000 x 2 = Rs. 32,000. The Trap: The position is a GAIN (not loss) because the price fell on a short. Rs. 16,000 is only one lot's MTM. Rs. 40 is the per-share gain, not the contract-level MTM. Note: Trap sentence repaired to read "A short position gains when the settlement price falls below the entry price."
